events.title: Birth of Martin Luther
events.description: Martin Luther was born in Eisleben, in the County of Mansfeld, Holy Roman Empire. He became an Augustinian monk and theologian who later challenged the practices of the Catholic Church.
events.significance: Luther's 95 Theses in 1517 sparked the Protestant Reformation, which reshaped Christianity, European politics, and culture.

events.title: Founding of the U.S. Marine Corps
events.description: The Continental Congress, meeting in Philadelphia, resolved to raise two battalions of marines to serve as landing forces with the fleet during the American Revolutionary War. The Marines trace their origins to Tun Tavern.
events.significance: This established the origin of the United States Marine Corps, which is celebrated annually on November 10 as the Marine Corps Birthday.

events.title: Stanley Meets Livingstone
events.description: Journalist and explorer Henry Morton Stanley found the missing Scottish missionary David Livingstone in Ujiji, near Lake Tanganyika, reportedly greeting him with the words 'Dr. Livingstone, I presume?'
events.significance: The meeting became one of the most famous episodes of European exploration in Africa and drew worldwide public attention to the continent.

events.title: Death of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
events.description: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, founder and first President of the Republic of Turkey, died at Dolmabahçe Palace in Istanbul at age 57.
events.significance: Atatürk led Turkey's War of Independence and implemented sweeping political, legal, and cultural reforms that modernized the country. Turkey observes a moment of silence each year on this date.

events.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall Begins
events.description: The day after East Germany opened its borders, crowds of East and West Germans gathered at the Berlin Wall, and people began dismantling sections of it with hammers and chisels while additional border crossings were opened.
events.significance: The dismantling of the Wall symbolized the collapse of communist rule in Eastern Europe and led to German reunification in 1990 and the end of the Cold War.
